propositions: The ADR-promised byte-total backstop trigger does not exist; _gc_pass reads only free disk space and mtime, never consulting _cache.byte_total, leaving no size-based reclaim mechanism despite the design contract
materialize_tickets populates tickets-<sha> entries (~620 MiB each, the dominant store consumer) without calling add_bytes, causing them to be invisible to the incremental byte-total counter
The snapshot store has no configurable size cap knob in the configuration surface, despite being promised as the primary backstop mechanism
On disk-constrained hosts the store grows unchecked because the free-space watermark trigger is unreachable below 93.3% disk usage and the missing byte-total cap is the only remaining trigger
cache.acquire correctly byte-accounts its entries but materialize_tickets bypasses acquire entirely, creating a second populate path that violates the incrementally-maintained accounting obligation
